segments.title: Opening: interview aims and Willie Humphrey, family friend
segments.summary: The interviewer explains he wants biographies and a feel for the time, mentioning musical families (Marrero, Barbarin, Humphrey). Eddie says Willie Humphrey is an old family friend and that the interviewer freelances for New Orleans Magazine.

segments.title: Starting on bass with the Golden Rule Band, c. 1918-19
segments.summary: Asked when he learned, Eddie says he started a year before his father died in 1919 and joined the Golden Rule Band around 1918-19.

segments.title: The Marrero brothers and father; Lawrence Marrero
segments.summary: The sibling lists the brothers (Simon, John, Aaron, Lawrence, Eddie). Eddie complains that writers ignore Simon, John and their father Billy Marrero, though Lawrence and George Lewis are known.

segments.title: Josiah Frazier and drum lessons
segments.summary: Eddie names Josiah Frazier; the interviewer took a few drum lessons from him. Eddie calls him among the best drummers, with Louis Barbarin.

segments.title: First band with Josiah, Lawrence and friends; Oil for Sale, 1924
segments.summary: The group Eddie started with is named: Josiah on drums, Raymond Brown on trombone, Bush Hall on cornet, Lawrence on banjo. They played together in 1924 before parting.

segments.title: Stopping music in 1928: low pay, marriage, odd jobs
segments.summary: Eddie says he stopped around 1928 when the pay fell to a dollar, he got a job and married. The sibling clarifies he later played only occasional odd jobs, never a regular band.

segments.title: Buddy Petit, Louis Armstrong and the Florida and Alabama trip
segments.summary: Eddie recalls Buddy Petit, close to Louis Armstrong, and a trip to Florida, then Montgomery, and an invitation to play block dances in Los Angeles around 1921 that he declined.

segments.title: Pete LaCache and the Supreme Band
segments.summary: Eddie asks whether anyone has told the interviewer about Pete LaCache, who played with the Supreme Band. The interviewer has not heard of him.

segments.title: Learning bass from brother Simon; Albert Morgan; the family biographies
segments.summary: Eddie says Simon taught him bass around 1918-19. The sibling shows the book entries on John, Simon and Lawrence, and Eddie is named only through his father.

segments.title: Playing before his father's death; Kid Rena
segments.summary: Eddie says he began before his father died in 1919 without playing in bands. After the death Simon took over, and Eddie praises Kid Rena as a cornetist.

segments.title: Who taught the brothers: father, Uncle Henry and the guitar
segments.summary: Simon learned bass from their father, Lawrence from John, and John from Uncle Henry, a guitarist from St. Mary Parish who taught him guitar, then mandolin, banjo and piano.

segments.title: Father's bands: Sam Morgan, Wooden Joe, Superior, Olympia
segments.summary: Eddie says his father quit and turned the band over to Sam Morgan, disputes that Wooden Joe played with him, and lists his father's bands, including Superior, Empire and Olympia with Bunk Johnson.

segments.title: Why he quit: the Depression and a dollar a night
segments.summary: Eddie says he quit around 1929 because of the Depression, when bands got a dollar a piece for nights lasting from 8 until morning.

segments.title: Last band: Young Tuxedo, Black Diamond Band and Jack Carey
segments.summary: Eddie says he last played with the Young Tuxedo band. He lists the Black Diamond Band's members, how the Island Queen job broke it up, and a cousin's reuse of the Golden Rule name. Jack Carey then took him to Montgomery.

segments.title: Rebutting stories about Louis Armstrong's learning
segments.summary: Eddie digresses to dispute accounts of how Louis Armstrong learned: the Waif's Home, Kid Ory, then Fate Marable at age 21. The sibling steers him back to his own career.

segments.title: Moving band to band; last band the Golden Rule, c. 1921-22
segments.summary: Eddie says he drifted from band to band with no regular one, his last being the Golden Rule around 1921-22 with the same group. He criticizes a book's claims about a manager.

segments.title: He never liked music; brothers did
segments.summary: The sibling steers him to his own career. Eddie says he never liked music and played only because of his brothers, who loved it and his father.

segments.title: Brothers died young; played music by force
segments.summary: Eddie lists his brothers' ages at death and says music did not shorten his life. He played by force, never loved it, unlike Lawrence and his father.

segments.title: Real career: cleaning, pressing and alterations
segments.summary: The sibling says Eddie's real profession was pressing and spot cleaning, which he did for 21 years until 1957 when failing blood forced him to stop.

segments.title: Lawrence stayed a musician; furniture store job and John's death
segments.summary: Lawrence never returned to cleaning and stayed a musician, taking odd jobs and a furniture store job around 1939. John died in 1942.

segments.title: How Lawrence drew him into the band
segments.summary: A group of boys, Josiah and Bush Hall among them, took up instruments, and Lawrence, who managed every band he played in, drew Eddie in. They played a first party for nothing.

segments.title: Admiring his brothers: Lawrence got him in
segments.summary: Eddie says Lawrence rather than Simon or John influenced him, since he was too young when they played. Lawrence showed him the music over about two years while working at a packing shop.

segments.title: Little interest, but liked traveling; not playing all night for a dollar
segments.summary: Eddie says he got little interest after joining but liked traveling, and would have gone to California if Lawrence had. The sibling says Lawrence was a wonderful banjoist. Eddie would not play all night for a dollar.

segments.title: Roosevelt, the CWA and regular band work again
segments.summary: Pay stayed a dollar until Roosevelt's election, when the CWA and similar programs brought regular band work at clubs for four dollars from eight to two.

segments.title: Enjoying people; marriage in 1930 and a dream about Lawrence
segments.summary: Eddie says he enjoyed seeing different people. The sibling dates his marriage to September 8, 1930, and recalls Lawrence playing around 1929 and a dream about Lawrence during an illness.

segments.title: Closing: article looking for 90-year-old musicians
segments.summary: An unidentified speaker and the interviewer talk about the magazine article, which seeks musicians about 90 years old.
